transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, hello doctor, thanks for seeing me today. I'm here because I keep forgetting my appointments and daily health stuff, even when I really try to stay on top of it. It's just gotten so hard to manage all these new medical routines lately, and it's starting to cause some real problems.
Along with the forgetfulness, have you been feeling down most days or lost interest in things you usually enjoy, or does this mainly seem tied to the stress of adjusting to your new medical routines?

Oh, I haven't been feeling down at all—in fact, I still love going to the senior center, organizing game nights, and helping my neighbors. The struggle is definitely tied to the stress of trying to manage all these new, strict medical routines and appointments since my heart scare. It's just really hard for me to keep track of all those schedules and daily tasks.

Did these memory and organization problems start only after your recent heart scare and the new medical routines, or were they happening before that too? Besides managing these health tasks, are they causing problems in other parts of your life, like conversations, finances, or getting around?

To be honest, I've always been this way—even back in grade school, my teachers sent notes home because I couldn't sit still or stop talking over others. It definitely affects other areas of my life now too, like letting folks down at the senior center when I forget my commitments, or constantly interrupting my nieces when they're trying to talk to me.

Have these attention and impulsivity problems been present pretty consistently throughout your life in different settings, like school, work, home, and relationships, or do they mainly get worse only during stressful periods like after your heart scare?

They've absolutely been with me my whole life, going all the way back to grade school when teachers complained about me roaming the classroom and talking over everyone. But it only became a major problem after my heart scare a year ago, because of the sudden, overwhelming amount of doctor visits and pill schedules I'm now expected to manage.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes lifelong symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity beginning in grade school and persisting across multiple settings, with current functional impairment. Symptoms are not better explained by depression and became more impairing recently due to increased organizational demands after a heart scare.
